deliverables.text: SEO Monitoring — Tech, Rankings, Schema, Indexing, Content

package_details.monthly_audit: Weekly scan for broken links, slow pages, missing meta tags, indexing issues, duplicate content, and schema errors. Issues flagged and prioritized for repair.
package_details.blog_or_seo: One blog post OR one full page SEO treatment per month. Your choice — send us your topic or a written draft by the 15th. If we don't hear from you by the 15th, we'll choose based on your best keyword opportunities. Deliverable live by the 22nd.
package_details.site_hour: One included hour of site work each month — used for updates you request or audit fixes that go beyond routine maintenance. Unused hours roll over and bank up month to month. They never expire.
package_details.quarterly_report: Every three months you'll receive a full performance report covering keyword rankings, traffic trends, what we've done, and what's coming next.
package_details.overage: Additional work beyond your banked hours is billed at $50/hr (our standard rate is $100/hr — you receive a 50% discount for the life of your package).

items.title: Schema Monitoring & Correction
items.why: WordPress and the Avada theme can silently overwrite structured data during page saves and plugin updates. Monitored monthly — re-applied when conflicts are detected.

items.title: Meta Description Monitoring
items.why: Plugin updates and WordPress changes can occasionally reset meta data across pages. Verified and corrected as part of monthly maintenance.

items.title: Indexing Monitoring
items.why: New content, plugin changes, and site updates can affect how Google crawls and indexes the site. Search Console reviewed monthly — coverage issues resolved as they arise.

items.title: Author Archive Pages — Noindex
items.why: WordPress generates author archive pages for every user account. These thin, auto-generated pages create duplicate content signals and expose internal admin structure to Google's index.

items.title: Blog Author Attribution
items.why: The IFS blog post is attributed to a behind-the-scenes admin account rather than a licensed therapist. Google's quality raters check author credentials on YMYL health content — this is a direct E-E-A-T liability.

items.title: Spam Filter + Contact Forms
items.why: SilentShield plugin was blocking all form submissions. Replaced with honeypot approach — both main contact and in-page booking forms verified working.

items.title: On-Site Testimonials
items.why: Patient testimonials are a direct trust signal that Google quality raters look for on YMYL health sites. The site currently has no testimonials section — a gap that affects perceived credibility.

items.title: Google Business Profile Optimization
items.why: GBP category alignment, service list, photos, and Q&A section all need a full optimization pass. A complete, verified profile is a hard requirement for local pack eligibility on therapy queries.

items.title: Psychology Today Profiles
items.why: Initial pass complete: 7 of 12 therapist Person schemas now include Psychology Today profile URLs. Remaining 5 (Jared, Clayton, Natalie, Mariah, Leah) need profile URLs — pending Kandy follow-up.

items.title: Privacy Policy & Terms of Service
items.why: Google quality raters check for trust pages on YMYL health sites. Once provided by the practice, these will be published and linked correctly across the site.

items.title: GBP Post Management
items.why: Regular GBP posts — blog excerpts, mental health tips, practice announcements — signal an active, engaged listing to Google and improve local pack visibility.

items.title: Google Review Process
items.why: Review count and average rating are direct local pack ranking factors. Growing toward 20+ reviews at 4.8+ average requires a consistent, compliant ask process — in-office or automated.

items.title: Priority Directory Submissions
items.why: TherapyDen, Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Bing Places, Apple Maps, and GoodTherapy — high-authority citations missing from the backlink profile. Each submission builds local authority and opens a new referral channel.

items.title: Location Landing Pages
items.why: Dedicated pages for Renton WA, Online Therapy Washington, and Online Therapy Arizona — each targeting location-specific search queries the site currently has no page to capture.

items.title: IFS Therapy Washington
items.why: 'IFS therapist renton wa', 'ifs therapist seattle', 'ifs therapy washington' — no indexed landing page. Zero SERP presence for the practice's primary keyword differentiator and strongest competitive advantage.

items.title: Anxiety Therapy Renton WA
items.why: 'Anxiety therapist renton wa' at pos 10.8 with 22 impressions and 0 clicks. Ranking but not capturing clicks without a dedicated page.

items.title: Couples Counseling Renton WA
items.why: 'Couples therapy renton' at pos 9.4 — page 1 threshold. High commercial intent keyword cluster with no dedicated landing page.

items.title: Depression Therapy Washington
items.why: Second most searched mental health condition after anxiety. Statewide keyword with no dedicated page — missed traffic across both in-person and telehealth service areas.

items.title: Trauma Therapy Washington
items.why: Supports the practice's trauma-specialized therapist team. High-empathy search cluster with strong conversion intent — searchers on this term are actively looking for help.

items.title: Online Therapy Washington & Arizona
items.why: 'Online therapy washington state' appearing with impressions and zero clicks. A single optimized page consolidates authority across both telehealth service states.

items.title: Family Therapy Renton WA
items.why: Completes the core service page library. Without it the practice has no indexed page for family therapy queries despite offering the service.

items.title: FAQ Sections on All Service Pages
items.why: FAQ content qualifies pages for FAQ rich results in SERPs and directly addresses hesitant visitors. Every service page needs a FAQ section once built.

items.title: Internal Linking
items.why: Foundation work begun — bio-to-bio supervisory links and one bio→blog topical link (IFS) are live. Full execution waits for dedicated service pages to exist so each bio can link to a relevant service page.

messages.text: June package is active. May stats are in: 2,356 impressions (up 750 from last month), 141 keywords indexed (up 73), and 133 organic clicks. The big cleanup work from earlier in May — redirects, schema rebuilds, meta rewrites, FAQ noindex — continues to settle with Google and ranking improvements should become more visible over the next 4–6 weeks as Google re-crawls. The insurance blog published in May is indexed. This month your blog or SEO op slot is open — send your topic by June 15 and we'll have it live by the 22nd. If we don't hear from you we'll pick your best keyword opportunity from the current data. Quarterly performance report is scheduled for June 30.

Site maintenance session today covering two things. First: your contact form spam filter was rejecting real submissions with an error message — we replaced the old reCAPTCHA setup with a honeypot approach that stops bots without blocking clients. Both forms (main contact and the in-page booking form) are updated and tested. Second: fixed a layout issue on the Lori and Kristen bio pages — the hero card was rendering behind the navigation bar instead of below it, which was cutting off the top of each page. Root cause was a padding value set too low for the site's fixed header (155px tall). Updated both pages to match Jared's working layout, including the spacing between the schedule button and the bio card below it. All three therapist bios now match. (LOR-333)

Quick maintenance session this week. Fixed the contact forms on your site — a plugin called SilentShield was blocking all form submissions. Clients should now be able to reach you and your therapists without issues. Also updated session rates on Devi and Iwona's bio pages (correcting the listed fees). On the SEO side, cleaned up the About Our Therapists hero section: tightened the headline text, removed duplicate mentions of "online" and "Washington" that could flag as keyword stuffing, and polished the visual layout. (LOR-325, LOR-324, LOR-326)

Big SEO + schema cleanup pass on the site this afternoon. Twelve retired Avada portfolio URLs (cardiology, pediatrics, ultrasound — leftover from the old theme demo) were permanently deleted and 301-redirected to the Meet the Team page so any inbound links keep working and Google updates faster. We also closed the loop on three duplicate/old slugs (an old Ryan Carragher URL, plus former-therapist pages for Faynesha Haragan and Keziah Grindeland) — all redirected, no more 404s for Google. Three of the highest-impression pages got rewritten meta titles + descriptions tuned for click-through (Lori's bio, the contact page, and the Meet the Team page) — the bio page especially was sitting at 1,124 impressions with a 0.6% CTR, so we rebuilt the title around 'Online Therapist' service intent rather than IFS jargon. Roughly twenty thin auto-generated FAQ pages were noindex'd and pulled out of the sitemap — they were duplicating the FAQ schema already on the contact page and just cluttering Google's coverage report. We also rebuilt the Person schema on every therapist bio page so each one now has full credentials, license info, areas of focus, and Psychology Today links where they exist — Lori's bio correctly lists both Washington and Arizona service areas, all others are Washington-only. Added a sitewide WebSite + SearchAction schema (enables Google's sitelinks search box on brand searches), submitted the cleaned sitemap, and removed the redundant www GSC property. Everything is verified live. Real impact (CTR, indexing, ranking) will show in the next 4 weeks — checkpoint scheduled for June 7 to compare before/after.

This week we used Lori's included site hour to onboard the two new team members (Iwona Abraham and Devi Viswanathan) and update John Hubbs's credentials now that he's fully licensed. Both new therapists have full bio pages, and we added them to the homepage carousel, the Meet the Team page, the mega menu, the contact form dropdown, and the structured-data schema for Google. We also did a full SEO optimization pass on both new bios — single rich Person schema, focus keywords matching actual content, contextual internal links, sweet-spot meta lengths. While we were in there, we added Caroline Bacon to the contact form dropdown (she'd been missing since March), tightened up Jenn Kenworthy's specialty list per her request, fixed John's photo alignment on his Meet the Team card, and added one internal link from Lori's bio to the IFS blog post for SEO. Everything is live and verified.
